title: Snickers Apple Salad Is Definitely Dessert-and Nobody Minds
text:
1 days ago Snickers Apple Salad carries the word “salad” with a wink. Tart Granny Smith apples and chopped Snickers bars are folded into a fluffy mixture of vanilla pudding, cold milk, and whipped topping. The apples provide fresh crunch and acidity, while the candy contributes chocolate, peanuts, chewy nougat, and caramel. Each spoonful tastes creamy and sweet but includes enough crisp fruit to keep the texture lively. It requires no baking and only a handful of ingredients, making it one of those recipes that delivers far more attention than its preparation time would suggest.
Photo by Letisha Uber Bring it to barbecues, holiday dinners, picnics, potlucks, or family gatherings where dessert needs to travel easily. Homemade whipped cream can replace the prepared topping, and a drizzle of caramel sauce makes the bowl look especially indulgent. Add grapes, chopped pecans, miniature marshmallows, or extra peanuts for more texture. Prepare the creamy base ahead, but fold in the apples and candy closer to serving if you want maximum crunch. Keep the salad cold and provide a large spoon, because modest servings tend to become considerably larger once people taste it. Whether it appears beside the side dishes or waits on the dessert table, this sweet Midwest favorite rarely survives long enough to settle the category debate.
